purpose: Visual and microcopy comparison, not production strategy or live product availability.

copies.name: Always-on markets
copies.angle: Lead with the tension between market hours and an always-on token market.
copies.kicker: Sharper AMM LP. / FX + real-world assets
copies.headline: Sharper AMM LP.
copies.body: Market-aware liquidity for FX and tokenized assets. Define what happens when the reference market closes—and the on-chain market stays open.
copies.audience: FX · Tokenized assets · Issuers · Capital owners
copies.product: Put a strategy behind your liquidity.
copies.productBody: A market moves. Your inventory changes. The way a venue pays can change the value of every allocation. Bring those decisions into one operating view.
copies.markets: Two sides of the liquidity market.
pillars: A market close is a strategy input, not an afterthought.
Separate the token’s trading price from its external anchor.
Keep inventory, fees and operating costs in the same view.

copies.name: Asset-first liquidity
copies.angle: Help issuers recognize their asset before asking them to understand the architecture.
copies.kicker: Sharper AMM LP. / Built around the asset
copies.headline: Sharper AMM LP.
copies.body: A euro market is not a tokenized stock market. Start with the asset, its reference and its trading session. Shape the liquidity around them.
copies.audience: FX · Tokenized assets · Issuers · Capital owners
copies.product: Start with the assets you want to hold.
copies.productBody: A range is one decision. Your mandate also defines the asset mix, operating authority and benchmark. Keep them connected, without confusing fee income with the whole result.
copies.markets: Two sides of the liquidity market.
copies.close: Which asset are you building for?
copies.instrument: Concentration is a choice. Exposure is a consequence.
pillars: Place capital where the market needs it—not simply in the tightest ticks.
Set the assets you want to hold and the exposure you can accept.
Connect strategy, vault ownership and accountable operations.

copies.name: Engineering-led trust
copies.angle: Make session-aware market design tangible through a single readable engineering drawing.
copies.kicker: Sharper AMM LP. / Reference → policy → liquidity
copies.headline: Sharper AMM LP.
copies.lead: One market. Three signals. A clear policy.
copies.body: Reference value. Market session. Inventory. Connect them to explicit liquidity instructions, with strategy separate from on-chain custody and accounting.
copies.audience: FX · Tokenized assets · Issuers · Capital owners
copies.productBody: Where capital sits, when it moves and which assets it holds are connected decisions. Make the policy legible before judging its results.
copies.markets: Two sides of the liquidity market.
copies.instrument: A visible relationship. Not a return forecast.
pillars: Identify the source, quote currency and freshness rules.
Define open, closed and stale-input behavior before capital moves.
Apply an exposure policy; a reference price is not a guaranteed exit.

themes.name: Signal
themes.thesis: A financial poster with a living liquidity field.
themes.distinct: Monumental typography, a narrow editorial rail and a full-width liquidity interruption. Strategy entries become oversized numbered lines.
themes.tradeoff: The strongest brand recall, but the long headline needs careful mobile line breaks.
themes.prompt: Design a Swiss financial poster, not a software landing page. Interrupt monumental type with one meaningful liquidity field; carry the same strong rules and numbered rhythm through strategies and buyer stories.

themes.name: Caliper
themes.thesis: The range instrument is the product signature.
themes.distinct: A copy rail and a calibrated figure form one opening spread. Rulers, cross-references and open grid lines continue into every section.
themes.tradeoff: The mechanism is clearest here; the brand is quieter than the poster directions.
themes.prompt: Build a precision editorial instrument around two smooth liquidity envelopes. Put readable copy beside it, not on it. Use cobalt only for action and focus; maintain stable axes and explanatory labels.

themes.name: Contour
themes.thesis: Capital has a shape. Give it a landscape.
themes.distinct: A panoramic field stretches beneath a compact opening. Large contour lines and a continuous reading axis replace conventional feature boxes.
themes.tradeoff: Atmospheric and original; the schematic label must prevent an impression of real portfolio data.
themes.prompt: Treat liquidity as a continuous price landscape. Use a wide shallow figure, cream type on deep forest and copper contours. Keep samples subordinate to smooth envelopes and explain intent versus execution.

themes.name: Folio
themes.thesis: A product page with the authority of a considered journal.
themes.distinct: A restrained serif editorial lead, a numbered issue masthead and margin notes. Mechanism figures sit inside substantial reading spreads.
themes.tradeoff: Trustworthy reading rhythm; less immediate software energy than the technical entries.
themes.prompt: Create an asset owner’s journal with a Swiss grid, editorial serif leads, generous margins and concise figure captions. Explain the whole portfolio without turning the homepage into an academic paper.

themes.name: Dual
themes.thesis: Two institutional jobs make one product legible.
themes.distinct: One shared brand sits over two strongly divided buyer fields. A common mechanism reconnects them; selected focus changes context, not the product.
themes.tradeoff: Fast buyer recognition, at the cost of less first-screen engineering detail.
themes.prompt: Organize the opening as two institutional mandates: build an asset market and operate reserve assets. Use one brand and one primary call, with a single underlying liquidity mechanism.

themes.name: Section
themes.thesis: Separate decisions from ownership—and make the boundary beautiful.
themes.distinct: A cutaway diagram leads the right side; technical section lines and orange callouts explain strategy, vault and venue as different layers.
themes.tradeoff: The cleanest architecture story; commercial language must stay ahead of implementation detail.
themes.prompt: Draw a spare architectural cutaway of market inputs, strategy decisions, vault ownership and AMM execution. Never put signals in custody. Keep the first-screen proposition commercial, then reveal the system.

themes.name: Sequence
themes.thesis: One intentional transformation tells the product story.
themes.distinct: A centered typographic opening followed by a numbered Read / Shape / Run stage. Hard blue fields and stable alignments replace ambient animation.
themes.tradeoff: Distinctive and energetic; motion is optional and every stage must remain complete when paused.
themes.prompt: Use ultramarine as a confident editorial field. Show one intentional Read–Shape–Run transition with a stable axis and clear stage labels. No looping display, animated profits or scroll traps.

themes.name: Ledger
themes.thesis: A disciplined ledger makes complexity feel manageable.
themes.distinct: Horizontal rules, aligned definitions and a non-monetary position ledger. The whole page uses an accounting rhythm without fake balances.
themes.tradeoff: The most accountable story; deliberately less expressive than Signal or Contour.
themes.prompt: Build an operating ledger with no invented money. Separate assets, liquidity, trading fees, rewards and costs. Use a bold editorial opening and aligned rows; preserve a calm burgundy-and-paper identity.

themes.name: Nocturne
themes.thesis: Dark institutional restraint, without trading-terminal theatre.
themes.distinct: A quiet amber locator, deep negative space, inset research figure and full-width strategy reading panels. No glowing cards or tickers.
themes.tradeoff: Memorable and private; careful contrast is essential for long-form reading.
themes.prompt: Create a night research desk with charcoal, warm light and pale amber. Lead with huge calm typography, then a small precise figure. Avoid neon, tickers, gradients, glass and fake live market information.

themes.name: Workshop
themes.thesis: An invitation to shape a real liquidity mandate.
themes.distinct: A structured mandate slip sits beside the proposition. Choosing a buyer focus highlights useful inputs, then the page returns to product mechanics.
themes.tradeoff: Approachable and practical; the instrument keeps it from feeling like a consultancy questionnaire.
themes.prompt: Make an open professional workshop, not a lead-generation form. Pair a strong brand line with a small Assets / Market / Objective slip. Use disciplined green and a tangible schematic mechanism.

strategies.name: Optimal-Range
strategies.text: EMA and ATR connect recent market behavior to broad base liquidity and a focused allocation. Inventory policy shapes the final placement.

strategies.name: Follow-Tick
strategies.text: A tick-spaced focused range alongside the shared base and inventory policy. Aero-optimized design considers gauge eligibility, fees, reward claims and reinvestment costs together.

strategies.name: Vol+
strategies.text: Explore how market activity can inform dynamic fee design through Uniswap v4 hooks. The fee policy and the portfolio strategy remain separate.

strategies.name: Market-Aware
strategies.text: Bring external value, peg relationships and market sessions into the strategy design. LRT pairs need a moving exchange-rate reference—not an assumed fixed peg.

safety: Schematic product study. No live funds, forecasts or return claims. Strategy and venue availability are qualified for each mandate.
claimPolicy: Vision-led; no returns, TVL, testimonials, universal venue availability or audit claims. Strategy names follow the latest Commercial naming decision. No production APIs or booking transmissions.
scope: Static design review only. Does not edit the shared wireframe, canonical copy, application, contracts or strategy.
editorialModel: Ten design entries. Three copywriting directions assigned by fit. Alternate renders are retained for review, not presented as thirty competition entries.
